title: 6'''-Feruloylspinosin ameliorates pressure overload-induced heart failure with comorbid insomnia through the activation of RORalpha.
authors: Yan, Yan; Gong, Shuaishuai; Sun, Minhui; Huang, Zhekai; Gao, Lan; Li, Xinxin; Yu, Boyang; Kou, Junping; Du, Chenhui; Li, Fang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究6-FS激活RORalpha改善心衰伴失眠，虽含分子对接但核心为药物-蛋白作用，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Targeting the retinoid-related orphan receptor alpha (RORalpha) signalling pathway represents a promising therapeutic strategy for cardiovascular diseases comorbid with insomnia. Here, we identify 6'''-feruloylspinosin (6-FS) as a potent RORalpha activator and investigate its therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms in HF accompanied by insomnia. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Transverse aortic constriction (TAC) was conducted to induce heart failure comorbid with insomnia. Echocardiography, histopathology and serum biochemical indicators were examined. Transcriptomics analysis, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance binding assays, cellular thermal shift and microscale thermophoresis assays were performed. Subsequently, the mechanisms underlying 6-FS-mediated protection were elucidated through Western blot (WB), immunofluorescence (IF) and immunohistochemistry (IHC). KEY RESULTS: 6'''-Feruloylspinosin (6-FS) effectively improved cardiac function and mitigated myocardial injury in the mice model of TAC-induced HF. 6-FS attenuated pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy and significantly improved insomnia and anxiety-like behaviours through modulation of neurotransmitter systems. 6-FS ameliorated insomnia through restoration of tight junction integrity and suppression of neuroinflammation. Mass spectrometry analysis confirmed the presence of 6-FS in both cardiac and cerebral tissues, and transcriptomic analysis demonstrated a marked up-regulation of RORalpha following 6-FS administration. Mechanistically, 6-FS exhibited the strongest binding affinity for RORalpha and simultaneously enhanced RORalpha-mediated regulation of the JAK2/STAT3 signalling pathway. Importantly, RORalpha inhibition completely abrogated the protective effects of 6-FS against TAC-induced cardiac hypertrophy and insomnia. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Our findings highlight 6-FS as a novel RORalpha activator with dual cardioprotective and sleep-enhancing benefits, offering new insights into the prevention and treatment of cardiovascular diseases with comorbid sleep disturbances.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：靶向维A酸相关孤儿受体α（RORalpha）信号通路是治疗心血管疾病伴失眠的一种有前景的策略。在此，我们鉴定出6'''-阿魏酰斯皮诺素（6-FS）作为一种强效的RORalpha激活剂，并研究其在心力衰竭（HF）伴失眠中的治疗效果及潜在机制。实验方法：采用横向主动脉缩窄（TAC）诱导心力衰竭伴失眠模型。检查超声心动图、组织病理学和血清生化指标。进行转录组学分析、分子对接、表面等离子体共振结合实验、细胞热位移和微量热泳动实验。随后，通过蛋白质印迹（WB）、免疫荧光（IF）和免疫组织化学（IHC）阐明6-FS介导保护作用的机制。关键结果：6'''-阿魏酰斯皮诺素（6-FS）有效改善了TAC诱导的HF小鼠模型中的心脏功能并减轻了心肌损伤。6-FS减轻了压力超负荷诱导的心脏肥大，并通过调节神经递质系统显著改善了失眠和焦虑样行为。6-FS通过恢复紧密连接完整性和抑制神经炎症来改善失眠。质谱分析确认了6-FS在心脏和脑组织中的存在，转录组学分析显示6-FS给药后RORalpha显著上调。机制上，6-FS对RORalpha表现出最强的结合亲和力，并同时增强RORalpha介导的JAK2/STAT3信号通路调控。重要的是，RORalpha抑制完全消除了6-FS对TAC诱导的心脏肥大和失眠的保护作用。结论与意义：我们的发现强调6-FS作为一种新型RORalpha激活剂，具有双重心脏保护和睡眠增强益处，为心血管疾病伴睡眠障碍的预防和治疗提供了新见解。
